summary: Lotus's first SUV is a 2.5-tonne, 450kW-to-675kW electric hyper-SUV that Australian reviewers rate genuinely well — CarExpert called it "really, ridiculously good" and praised air suspension that stays composed on coarse country roads — but CarsGuide scored it only 7.2 out of 10 and flagged limited cabin practicality and a driving character that no longer resembles a Lotus. A MY25 factory price cut of $49,010 to $35,010 a variant transformed the value case, dropping the entry car from $239,000 to $189,990, and it is that repricing rather than the engineering that reviewers now credit for making it competitive. The unresolved risk is ownership rather than the car: Lotus sold 12 Eletres in Australia in 2024, nine in 2025 and three to date in 2026, through a five-showroom network, so parts, resale and service depth are all unproven.
pros: Cut by $49,010 in MY25 — the entry Eletre fell from $239,000 to $189,990 before on-roads, undercutting a BMW iX M60 and Lamborghini Urus while offering 450kW and 4.5sec to 100km/h
800V architecture takes 350kW DC for a 10-80 per cent charge in about 20 minutes, well ahead of the 400V Audi SQ8 e-tron and Mercedes-AMG EQE SUV it is cross-shopped against
688-litre boot expanding to 1,532 litres and a 2,250kg braked tow rating, which is more than the BMW iX or Polestar 3 will pull
CarExpert rates the Unreal Engine 5 infotainment as "one of the best infotainment experiences available", ahead of Tesla's, backed by a 23-speaker 2,160W KEF system on the S
Two-year/30,000km service intervals with only cabin filter and brake fluid as mandatory replacements, so scheduled maintenance is unusually light for the price bracket
cons: CarExpert recorded 340km from a full charge in hard driving against a 490km WLTP claim on the R, so the 600km and 535km figures on these grades will not survive highway use
Lotus has no capped-price servicing in Australia and distributes through only five Simply Sports Cars showrooms, so warranty and repair access is thin outside the capitals
Resale is the weakest part of the case: 24 Eletres were sold new in Australia across 2024 and 2025 combined, and the MY25 price cut wiped up to $49,010 off MY24 cars overnight
Standard brakes are judged inadequate for the performance — CarExpert recommends the $32,199 carbon-ceramic upgrade, and options escalate a car that already carries heavy unrecoverable Luxury Car Tax
The flagship Eletre R at $279,990 sits above this calculator's modelling ceiling, and neither S nor base qualifies for the FBT exemption, so novated leasing offers no relief on any grade
